description: Price wicks through a BSL pool and closes back below it. Penetration plus rejection close is a sweep, confirmed on that same close.
labelling_rationale: SLS §4.6 step 1 requires penetration H[i] > Pl + e, and step 2 requires a rejection close Cl[i] < Pl; step 3 says the sweep then confirms immediately at that close as a single-candle sweep. The series carries a confirmed internal swing high of 106 at index 2 (k_int = 2 per §3.1), which §4.2 turns into a BSL pool once the swing confirms at index 4. Candle 6 has high 109 and closes at 104. Per §0.4 the tolerance is e = 0.05 x ATR(14); the true ranges of candles 0..6 are 2, 2, 4, 3, 2, 2, 6, summing to 21 over 7 candles, so ATR = 3 exactly and e = 0.15. Penetration holds because 109 > 106.15, and the rejection close holds because 104 < 106, so the pool transitions ACTIVE -> SWEPT with sweep_depth = (109 - 106) / 3 = 1 ATR. The candle opened at 104, below the level, so gap_sweep is false (§4.6 Edge Case 4). A second pool exists: the confirmed internal swing low of 101 at index 4 becomes an SSL pool at index 6, but its lifecycle scan would start at index 7 which is past the end of the series, so it stays ACTIVE and untouched. Pool strength follows §4.2's four-component formula: touches 0 gives 0, H1 is rank 3 of 6 giving 12.5, age 2 candles gives 25 x 2 / 200 = 0.25, and a single-swing pool gives cluster 6.25 — total 19.00 for the BSL pool and 18.75 for the newer SSL pool whose age component is 0. Candle numbers above are scenario-relative; the 293 declared filler candles (SLS §1.9 warm-up) shift them by 293 in the expected output. The filler's height is deliberately 3, equal to the scenario's mean true range, so the blended 14-period ATR lands on exactly 3 at the confirming candle just as it did before history was declared — every threshold in this rationale therefore still holds unchanged. Its high matches the scenario's first candle so the seam cannot form a swing high, and its low sits below so it cannot form a swing low. ATR is Wilder's smoothing (SLS §2), not a simple mean: the long filler run of constant true range 3 converges ATR to exactly 3, then the scenario's true ranges 2, 2, 4, 3, 2, 2, 6 smooth it forward one candle at a time to 3.044374172402048223347171914 at the confirming candle. Sweep depth is therefore 3 / that = 0.9854242054724053640232107909 and epsilon 0.05 x that = 0.1522187086201024111673585957, both recorded quantised to 4 places per §0.4's derived-precision rule. Comparisons use the unquantised values, so no verdict depends on the rounding.
